---
title: "Methods, scope, and review roles"
---

## What the evidence represents

The [learning edition](learn/index.qmd) reorganizes five completed studies and
four selected archived nominal differential-pair/OTA cases into a connected
reading route. It is not a sixth completed research campaign. Existing study
freezes, exposed inputs and definitions remain unchanged. The new
[learning package](studies/learning-path-v1/reproduce.qmd) labels its selected
source identities, actual readback, leaf reanalysis and native replay scope.
The old zero-raw `ARTIFICIAL` realizations are nominal interventions; old v2
noise and settling definitions remain distinguishable from new calculations.
No selected-D1 25-pF transfer, final mirror correction or paused self-bias
performance is borrowed to complete the route.

The first study combines explicit calculations, nominal SPICE observations,
controlled interventions, a fixed local prediction model and a prospective
confirmation using saved physical realizations. These roles are labelled in
the guide. An equation populated with an observed nominal operating point is
a retrospective explanation. A forecast saved before a new target is observed
is prospective, even when its local Jacobian was learned from earlier SPICE.

The passive study reuses the first study's already exposed MOS cohort. Its new
resistance conditions and predictions were frozen before those targets, but it
does not call the MOS samples fresh. The common/ratio log-error scenarios are
explicitly synthetic and separate from the APM Local profile. Exact finite
cohort comparisons, hard functional counts and approximation errors are reported
without a new manufacturing-yield or population-confirmation claim.

The pinned public device source is
[APM v5.0.0, commit 381517f](https://github.com/ds54e/analog-process-models/tree/381517fda5107fabf98af7801d5a5103f38e230c).
APM045 VTG uses native BSIM4 in ngspice 47. Its Local profile is a
**source-transfer hypothesis** based on a TSMC40 companion adaptation, with an
independent-Croon covariance assumption and a drawn-area geometry transfer.
See the pinned [source decision](https://github.com/ds54e/analog-process-models/blob/381517fda5107fabf98af7801d5a5103f38e230c/validation/evidence/v5_source_decision.md).

The profile does not establish global/spatial/passive variation, calibrated
weak-inversion or temperature/noise statistics, manufacturing yield, TSMC55
correlation or silicon qualification. Increasing the number of simulated
coordinates cannot remove unquantified model-transfer uncertainty. The study
has no layout/PEX or integrated-regulator validation.

## Checks and their limits

Numerical usability requires finite complete observations, the expected solver,
actual model/geometry/raw-parameter readback and terminal-domain checks.
Specification performance is evaluated separately; failed physical designs
remain in the denominator. No individual circuit is trimmed or recentered to
meet a common target.

The first study completed all 3,712 frozen condition attempts and checked their
file/model identities and physical readbacks. Forty full saved-data assessments
were recomputed exactly. Two representative numerical refinements and earlier
analytic resistor/RC and measurement-edge checks support the implementation.
The public package provides compact data, exact circuit bodies, saved raw
physical values, definitions and selected replay commands. Bulk calibration
and waveform archives are not required to run those selected replays.

See the [public evidence receipt](studies/gain-operating-point-accuracy/evidence.json),
[measurement definitions](studies/gain-operating-point-accuracy/measurements-v1.json)
and [frozen protocol](studies/gain-operating-point-accuracy/confirmation-plan.json).
The twelve exploratory coordinates remain separate from the 464 confirmation
coordinates. Available historical exposure was audited; deleted older raw
records cannot support an exhaustive uniqueness claim.

The [passive evidence receipt](studies/passive-sensitivity/evidence.json)
records 5,568 new transfer conditions and 156 nominal controls. Every scalar
assessment and physical readback was rechecked. All are numerically usable and
terminal-supported; physical specification failures remain in the public data.
Its public-only example reproduced six graphs, all summary calculations and two
selected native passive-condition observations in a fresh Python/model checkout
on the same host. No full-campaign or clean-OS replay is implied.

The [allocation evidence](studies/active-allocation/evidence.json) records
7,176 fresh physical conditions and the finite nominal/cause checks behind its
same-current/area comparison. All saved physical identities and scalar
measurements were rechecked. Useful-effect thresholds and inconclusive results
remain separate from merely positive estimated differences.

The [feedback evidence](studies/finite-feedback/evidence.json) records
4,168 main conditions on 521 fresh paired coordinates and 24 preselected 20-mV
sine conditions. Its 33-attempt nominal dynamic block includes an analytic
RC control, finite ramps with independent DC targets, actual current/charge
checks and targeted refinements. The input source's signed current, enlarged
resistor budget and changed signal/load requirements are explicit. A sparse
waveform subset establishes no dynamic population rate or formal loop stability.
All eleven public figures/statistics and four preselected native examples were
checked in a fresh public model/Python environment on the same host.

The [power-sequencing evidence](studies/power-sequencing/evidence.json) covers
59 fixed nominal static/PWL/control observations on unchanged saved circuits.
Zero-voltage sources are driven/clamped; floating I/O and a real driver are
outside that comparison. The original entry-into-band measurement retains
already-in-band status separately from a resolved entry time. All saved inputs,
364 MOS unit uses, actual element/source values and scalar assessments were
rechecked. Five graphs/statistics and four retrospectively selected native
illustrations were reproduced from public inputs. This establishes neither
new Local off-state statistics nor all-sequence startup behavior.

## AI and human roles

Codex performed the derivations, implementation, acquisitions, writing and
internal scientific/publication checks. The user selected the direction and
assesses the published results and chooses further directions. No prior human review,
peer approval or independent scientific validation is claimed. Reader
corrections can be reported through the public repository's Issues.

## Licensing

Original prose, plots and numerical data are **CC BY 4.0**. Original code and
circuit examples are **MIT**. Third-party software, fonts and retrieved models
retain their own terms. See the downloadable
[license mapping](licenses/LICENSE.md) and
[third-party notices](licenses/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

The public site is rendered with pinned Quarto 1.10.18. Its build copies
selected static resources and immutable versioned downloads; it never runs SPICE.
Graph regeneration and native replay are separate reader commands. Navigation,
equations, narrow layout, public assets and actual deployed revision are checked
as publication concerns, not additional scientific observations.
